events.objective: Establish the true onset time and blast radius of the customer-reported payment failures. Using query_logs and query_metrics, look at ALL payment-path signals between 12:00Z and 13:59Z, not just payment-service HTTP error_rate: transfer/transaction failure counts, retry counts, queue depth/lag, worker success/failure ratios, downstream call timeouts, and any 5xx/latency on non-HTTP or async paths. Determine (1) when failures actually began (compare to 12:17Z ≈ 15 min before report), (2) which services/endpoints show degradation, (3) whether the payment-service HTTP error_rate panel is scoped narrowly (single endpoint/instance/window) and masking failures elsewhere. Report concrete error signatures and counts.

Enumerate what changed and what is shared, across ALL services (not just payment-service), in the window 11:00Z–13:59Z. Using get_deployments and get_config_changes, list deploys/config changes for payment-service AND its dependencies; using get_service_dependencies, map payment-service's upstream/downstream graph (bank connector, broker, ledger, auth, DB) and identify shared components. Using search_historical_incidents, find precedents of 'green dashboard but real payment failures'. Flag any change whose timing could align with failure onset.

Correlate the changes found in task b against the precise failure onset time established in task a. Identify which specific deployment or config change (any service) temporally precedes and can explain the failures on the actual failing path, and whether it touches a shared component surfaced by the dependency graph. Conclude with the single most likely causal change or rule out all changes (pointing elsewhere), citing timestamps.

args.query: green dashboard but real payment failures error rate normal

events.statement: No deployments occurred in the incident window 11:00Z-13:59Z across all services (count 0). The only deploy in the wider 00:00Z-13:59Z window was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z ('Batch settlement report export', status live, not rolled back) -- a payments-org neighbor that shares ledger-db and kafka with payment-service.

Exactly one config change exists in 00:00Z-13:59Z: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000 -> 5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair, described as 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'. It affects payment-service itself and precedes the 12:32Z report.

payment-service dependency graph (edge = caller -> callee): api-gateway -> payment-service (http); payment-service -> ledger-db (db); payment-service -> bank-partner-api (external, has_telemetry=false); payment-service -> kafka (queue-produce). Shared components: ledger-db (postgres) and kafka, both marked shared=true; bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry.

ledger-db is a shared postgres used by four services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service; kafka is a shared queue used by order-service (produce), payment-service (produce), settlement-service (consume) and notification-service (consume). A fault in either shared component can therefore propagate to payment-service from a neighbor.

Historical precedent search returned no incident matching 'green dashboard but real payment failures'. Closest matches are dependency_failure precedents: HIST-105 (2025-11-19, 'Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes', payment-service payment failures) and HIST-103 (2025-10-21, external exchange API outage causing upstream timeouts); other matches were credential_expiry (HIST-106), bad_deployment/auth regression (HIST-109) and ledger-db resource_exhaustion (HIST-114). The tool notes these are 'leads, not evidence about the current incident'.

Timing alignment: the only change in the window (cfg-2502, bank timeout 3000->5000 at 11:20:00Z) sits between the settlement-service deploy at 10:30:00Z and the 12:32:00Z report of ~40 failed-transfer tickets 'in the last 15 minutes', so failure onset (~12:17Z) is ~57 minutes after the config change and ~2 hours after the deploy -- neither is tightly co-located with onset.

events.description: No telemetry exists for bank-partner-api (has_telemetry=false in tc-005), so I could not check partner-side latency/error changes or confirm whether the partner advisory behind cfg-2502 corresponds to real partner degradation.

Budget ran out before querying available_metrics and timeseries for shared components (ledger-db, kafka) and for api-gateway/settlement-service to see whether a shared-component signal shifted at ~12:17Z.
Deployment history was only queried for 2026-04-02 (00:00Z onward); no rollbacks were observed in that range but earlier days were not checked.

events.answer: Across ALL services in 11:00Z-13:59Z there were ZERO deployments and exactly ONE config change: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000->5000 ms at 11:20:00Z (cfg-2502, 'after partner advisory'). The only nearby deploy is settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z (live, not rolled back). payment-service sits behind api-gateway and depends on ledger-db (shared postgres, 4 services), kafka (shared queue, 4 services) and bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry). No historical precedent matches the 'green dashboard but real payment failures' pattern; the nearest precedents are external dependency failures (HIST-105 bank 5xx, HIST-103 exchange outage) and one ledger-db capacity incident (HIST-114). The 11:20Z timeout change and 10:30Z deploy are the only change candidates, but neither is tightly aligned with the ~12:17Z failure onset.

events.statement: payment-service HTTP error_rate (unit: '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)') stayed completely flat and normal across the entire incident window: 0.23% at 12:00Z, 0.21% at 12:15Z, 0.19% at 12:20Z, min 0.1 / mean 0.22 over 120 points. This is why the dashboard stayed green while payments failed.

The narrow HTTP 5xx panel masked the real failure because the failing path is not returning HTTP 5xx: bank_api_error_rate on payment-service jumps from 0.21% at 12:10Z to exactly 100.0% in the 12:15Z bucket (and stays 100.0% through 13:55Z), while payment_success_rate collapses from 99.41% (12:10Z) to 2.45% (12:15Z) and averages ~2.5% for the rest of the window.

True onset is the 12:15Z metric bucket (5-min granularity, so failures began between 12:10Z and 12:15Z), earlier than the report's 12:17Z guess. The first concrete error log is a payment marked PENDING_RETRY at 12:15:27Z, and the explicit cert-expiry signature appears at 12:16:44Z.

Concrete error signatures and counts in payment-service logs (12:00–13:59Z): 313 total matched WARN/ERROR (311 ERROR, 2 WARN), dominated by two patterns — 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' x171 (first 12:16:44Z) and 'payment <id> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' x140 (first 12:15:27Z). Logs continue to the latest data at 13:58:39Z.

The failing signature is a client-side mTLS certificate the client itself presents: cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal with notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. Its expiry timestamp coincides exactly with the start of the 12:15Z failure bucket. The remote bank error is 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'.

Blast radius appears confined to the payment→bank-partner-api path: settlement-service shows only benign signals in the window (3 WARN total — 2 GC pauses and 1 NTP clock drift, none payment-related), i.e. no propagation signature there. bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no logs/metrics of its own (its callers must be observed instead).

events.description: Tool-call budget was exhausted before I could query kafka for queue depth/lag or query payment-service latency_p99_ms, so the async/queue-side blast radius and request latency impact are unmeasured.
bank-partner-api is an external dependency: 'we have no logs/metrics for it. Observe it through its callers.'
payment-worker and payment-queue are not valid service names (known_services list has no such entries); the worker/queue layer is presumably inside payment-service or kafka.
Metric buckets are 5 minutes, so onset is bounded to the interval (12:10Z, 12:15Z] rather than an exact second; exact onset second unconfirmed.

events.answer: Failures began at ~12:15Z (the 12:15Z 5-min bucket; first error log 12:15:27Z), roughly 2 minutes earlier than the report's 12:17Z guess — and they are still ongoing at 13:58Z. The payment-service HTTP error_rate panel is green because it only counts HTTP 5xx and the real path fails at the TLS/mTLS layer: bank_api_error_rate went 0.21%→100% while payment_success_rate fell 99.4%→2.5%. The signature is 171 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' and 140 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' errors, caused by the client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expiring at exactly 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. Blast radius looks confined to the payment→bank-partner-api path; settlement-service shows no related degradation.

events.statement: In the tight window around the 12:15Z failure onset (11:50:00Z–12:30:00Z), there were zero deployments and zero config changes across all services, i.e. no change coincides with onset.

Across 2026-04-01T00:00Z–2026-04-02T13:59Z only one config change exists: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000 -> 5000 at 11:20:00Z by p.nair ('Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'). It is a timeout value on the bank call, not a cert/credential or endpoint change.

The only nearby deploy is settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z ('Batch settlement report export', status live, /rolled_back_at: null/), ~105 min before onset and not rolled back; deployment list for settlement-service confirms no other deploy.

Timing alignment: cfg-2502 (11:20:00Z) precedes the 12:15Z onset by ~55 min and the only deploy (10:30:00Z) by ~105 min; neither is co-located with onset, so neither can explain a failure that starts exactly at 12:15:00Z.

The failing path payment-service -> bank-partner-api does sit in a graph with shared components: payment-service -> ledger-db (db), -> kafka (queue-produce); ledger-db and kafka are both marked shared=true, while bank-partner-api (the branch that actually failed) is external with has_telemetry=false.

Historical precedent HIST-106 (2025-06-30, category credential_expiry, settlement-service) matches the current failure category: 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation' with symptoms 'tls handshake failures','expired certificate'. This is a lead only, not evidence about the current incident.

events.description: Could not locate any change (deploy, config, or cert-rotation record) for the payments client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal itself; change-history tools expose only app config and deployments, not PKI/cert lifecycle records.
bank-partner-api is external with has_telemetry=false, so no logs/metrics of its own were available.

events.answer: No deployment or config change temporally precedes or explains the ~12:15Z payment failures. In a tight window around onset (11:50–12:30Z) there were ZERO deploys and ZERO config changes, and the full window contains only one config change (cfg-2502, payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000 at 11:20:00Z) and one nearby deploy (settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z) — both ~55–105 min before onset and neither touching the failing path. All changes can therefore be ruled out; the failures are best explained by the client mTLS certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) expiring exactly at onset — a credential-expiry event, not a change. The failing path (payment-service → bank-partner-api) does touch a shared-component graph, but bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry; the shared ledger-db/kafka were not implicated by any change.

Shared dependency (ledger-db or kafka) degraded by the 10:30Z settlement-service v1.9.0 deploy, propagating into payment-service
External bank-partner-api degraded (dependency_failure), failing payment transfers
